independence.scope_note: Only the active M7_sol Daniel baseline, Daniel strategy, Gen/Exod/Lev quality bar, canonical WEB Daniel, and local OSHB/UXLC Daniel source views were used. M1-M6, comparison, and T417 layers were not read.

web.use: received 66-book English coordinates and immediate discourse context

oshb.use: MT order, Hebrew/Aramaic surface, morphology, qere/ketiv tags, and open/closed section markers as evidence only

uxlc.use: accented WLC-family surface plus qere/ketiv and section-marker crosscheck only

source_scope.correlation_warning: OSHB and UXLC are correlated Leningrad/WLC-family derivatives, not two independent textual witnesses.
source_scope.roots_guard: Lemma attributes, Strong-style identifiers, and roots are lookup evidence only. No gloss, semantic range, etymology, or boundary is inferred from a root or identifier.

source_gaps: No local primary Old Greek Daniel, Theodotion Daniel, Greek-addition text, or critical apparatus was available; no Greek wording, order, length, or reading claim is simulated.
No local primary Qumran Daniel transcription or apparatus was available; no fragment-supported reading or boundary is claimed.
No local primary Syriac, Vulgate, independent Hebrew/Aramaic manuscript, or qualified textual-critical apparatus was available.
No local qualified Hebrew/Aramaic syntax commentary, lexicon, rabbinic corpus, Second Temple corpus, or ANE comparison corpus was available; no reception or historical claim is invented.

versification_crosswalk.scope: reference-label alignment only; never boundary, canon, witness, or preferred-reading authority
versification_crosswalk.boundary_warning: The WEB 5:30|5:31 and 5:31|6:1 seams do not coincide with the MT chapter division; both alternatives must remain explicit.

language_transition_guard.hebrew_to_aramaic: Aramaic direct speech begins inside WEB/MT Dan.2.4 after the Hebrew adverb אַרָמִית. Verse-only coordinates cannot represent 2:4a|2:4b without inventing a half-verse object.
language_transition_guard.aramaic_to_hebrew: Dan.8.1 resumes Hebrew after the Aramaic vision closes at Dan.7.28.
language_transition_guard.use: The language transitions corroborate macro architecture only and authorize no authorship, date, source-layer, history, or canon conclusion.

reviews.literary_form: court-entry exposition and renaming register
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The dated וַיְהִי opening, vessel transfer, royal selection command, four-name catalogue, and imposed-name list form the intake scene; וַיָּשֶׂם דָּנִיֵּאל עַל־לִבּוֹ at 1:8 begins Daniel's counter-action.
reviews.counterevidence: The ration is introduced at 1:5 and therefore anticipates the test, but anticipation does not erase the new subject-volition and request at 1:8.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject splitting 1:1-2 from 1:3-7 merely to isolate chronology, and reject merging through 1:16 merely because food appears in both movements.
translation_and_textual_risks: Dan.1.4 carries correlated OSHB/UXLC qere/ketiv pressure (MT ketiv מאום); it affects wording, not the 1:7|1:8 seam.
Names, titles, and court vocabulary do not authorize etymology, identity, history, or chronology.

reviews.literary_form: food-test scene followed by enablement/examination coda
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The request-test-result chain closes at 1:16. Verse 17 resets the subject to all four youths and the divine gifts, then proceeds to the appointed-time examination, service, and Cyrus tenure notice.
reviews.counterevidence: Both movements complete the chapter-one formation tale, so Dan.1.1-21 should remain a mandatory macro parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer retrievable children Dan.1.8-16 and Dan.1.17-21 under Dan.1.1-21; reject one undifferentiated 1:8-21 unit.
translation_and_textual_risks: The senses of יִתְגָּאַל and the food terms are clause-bound and do not decide ritual or ethical questions.
Dan.1.21 is chronology-bearing narrative closure, not permission to harmonize regnal dates.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should 1:8-16 and 1:17-21 surface as hydrated children while the full 1:1-21 court-entry parent remains mandatory?

reviews.literary_form: dream-demand crisis and lethal decree
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The dated disturbance, summons, repeated demand-response exchanges, impossibility claim, and decree reaching Daniel form one escalating crisis. The Aramaic switch occurs inside 2:4 and cannot become a verse boundary.
reviews.counterevidence: The royal exchange contains several speech turns, but each intensifies the same demand and closes only when the decree goes out at 2:13.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject 2:4a|2:4b as a chunk coordinate and reject atomizing each king-wise-men exchange.
translation_and_textual_risks: MT qere/ketiv tags occur at 2:4, 2:5, 2:9, and 2:10 in both correlated views.
אַרָמִית marks the language of the following speech, not an authorship or source stratum.

reviews.literary_form: intervention scene followed by communal petition, revelation, and hymn
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: בֵּאדַיִן דָּנִיֵּאל introduces Daniel's intervention at 2:14; אֱדַיִן דָּנִיֵּאל לְבַיְתֵהּ אֲזַל at 2:17 changes location and participants. MT places a pe after 2:16, corroborating the scene-to-prayer transition.
reviews.counterevidence: The time request enables the prayer and revelation, so both children require the complete 2:14-23 crisis-response parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer Dan.2.14-16 plus Dan.2.17-23 as hydrated children; reject treating intervention and the prayer-hymn as one form.
translation_and_textual_risks: Dan.2.22 contains correlated qere/ketiv pressure on the light term; it does not alter the 2:16|2:17 seam.
The hymn is not detached as an abstract doctrinal proof text.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should the pe-supported 2:14-16 intervention and 2:17-23 prayer-revelation-hymn be separate retrieval children with mandatory sibling hydration?

reviews.literary_form: court presentation containing dream report and interpretation
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The Arioch presentation and Daniel's disclaimer lead into אַנְתְּ מַלְכָּא חָזֵה הֲוַיְתָ at 2:31; דְּנָה חֶלְמָא וּפִשְׁרֵהּ נֵאמַר at 2:36 explicitly joins report and interpretation in one answer.
reviews.counterevidence: MT section marks after 2:24 and 2:28 and the report/interpretation formula at 2:36 permit subordinate children, but severing the report from its interpretation would weaken context.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 2:24-45 as the retrieval unit; if children are added, prefer 2:24-30 and 2:31-45 rather than isolating 2:31-35 from 2:36-45.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 2:26, 2:33, and 2:38-43.
The metals, stone, and kingdom language authorize no identity, chronology, fulfillment, or theology.

reviews.literary_form: recognition and promotion coda
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The completed interpretation triggers the king's response, confession, gifts, Daniel's promotion, and the companions' appointments; the pe after 2:49 closes the tale.
reviews.counterevidence: The response depends on 2:24-45, so the full chapter remains a macro parent even though the coda is formally distinct.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject merging the response into the interpretation speech and reject splitting each promotion.
translation_and_textual_risks: Court gestures and titles are described, not interpreted as theology or ritual prescription.
No independent versional evidence is locally available to adjudicate wording.

reviews.literary_form: image dedication, herald decree, and compliance scene
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The image, assembled officials, herald command, repeated instrument list, sanction, and collective compliance form one court spectacle; כָּל־קֳבֵל דְּנָה בֵּהּ־זִמְנָא at 3:8 begins the accusation.
reviews.counterevidence: The lists are internally repetitive, but repetition performs the decree and must not be atomized.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject splitting the officials, instruments, sanction, and compliance into list chunks.
translation_and_textual_risks: Loanword spellings and qere/ketiv tags at 3:3, 3:5, and 3:7 are correlated WLC evidence only.
No local OG/Theodotion text exists to support a wording or length claim.

reviews.literary_form: accusation and confrontation dialogue
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The accusation at 3:8 restates the decree, summons the three, and advances through royal threat and their direct answer; a samekh after 3:18 and the king's fury at 3:19 close the confrontation.
reviews.counterevidence: A samekh after 3:12 distinguishes accusation from confrontation, but the accusation exists to trigger the hearing and remains short.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 3:8-18; reject detaching 3:8-12 from the answer unless a mandatory confrontation parent is provided.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 3:10, 3:12, 3:15, and 3:18.
The answer is preserved in context without deciding miracle, ethics, or application.

reviews.literary_form: furnace peril, witnessed deliverance, decree, and promotion
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: בֵּאדַיִן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הִתְמְלִי חֱמָא initiates execution; the sequence proceeds through casting, astonishment, summons, inspection, blessing, decree, and promotion to the pe after 3:30.
reviews.counterevidence: Pe/samekh marks after 3:23 and 3:25 distinguish execution and royal reaction, while 3:28-30 is a proclamation coda; all remain outcome phases of one peril-deliverance arc.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain the complete 3:19-30 resolution; do not isolate the fourth-figure description, decree, or promotion.
translation_and_textual_risks: Qere/ketiv tags at 3:19, 3:21, 3:25, 3:26, 3:28, and 3:29 do not select identities or readings.
No local Greek textual evidence supports claims about additions, order, or the fourth figure.

reviews.literary_form: royal proclamation address and hymnic thesis
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: MT Dan.3.31-33 contains the addressee, peace greeting, testimonial purpose, and kingdom/dominion thesis; WEB 4:4/MT 4:1 resets with אֲנָה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר and a first-person palace setting.
reviews.counterevidence: These verses frame the whole chapter-four proclamation and must remain connected to the dream-realization-restoration parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain WEB 4:1-3 as a formal opening; reject treating the WEB chapter label as the MT coordinate.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 4:1-3 equals MT 3:31-33; versification is metadata, not a boundary authority.
Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur in MT 3:31-32.

reviews.literary_form: first-person royal dream report
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: WEB 4:4/MT 4:1 opens first-person tranquility, then disturbance, failed court interpretation, Daniel's arrival, tree vision, watcher decree, and explicit interpretation request.
reviews.counterevidence: The arrival of Daniel and the watcher speech are internal scene and speech changes, but the king presents them as one dream report.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject splitting the tree image from the embedded decree or the request that completes the report.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 4:4-18 maps to MT 4:1-15.
Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at MT 4:4, 4:9, and 4:13-15; person and title renderings remain evidence only.

reviews.literary_form: dream interpretation and closing counsel
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: WEB 4:19/MT 4:16 resets with Daniel's stunned silence and dialogue; identification, decree explanation, duration formula, and counsel proceed as one answer through WEB 4:27/MT 4:24.
reviews.counterevidence: The counsel in the last verse is paraenetic rather than explanatory, but it is explicitly Daniel's conclusion to the interpretation.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Reject detaching WEB 4:27 from the interpretation or merging the answer with the subsequent realization.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 4:19-27 maps to MT 4:16-24.
Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at MT 4:16, 4:19, 4:21, and 4:24; time and counsel wording do not authorize chronology or ethics.

reviews.literary_form: fulfillment hinge, realization narrative, and restoration doxology
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: WEB 4:28/MT 4:25 is the formula כֹּלָּא מְּטָא and ends with a pe. WEB 4:29 begins the twelve-month realization scene; WEB 4:34 resets to first person with וְלִקְצָת יוֹמַיָּא and restored praise.
reviews.counterevidence: All three movements complete one dream-fulfillment-restoration arc, so WEB 4:28-37 remains a mandatory parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer WEB 4:28 as a hinge attached to the preceding interpretation or parent, WEB 4:29-33 as realization, and WEB 4:34-37 as restoration/doxology; at minimum split 4:28-33 from 4:34-37.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 4:28-37 maps to MT 4:25-34.
Qere/ketiv tags at MT 4:29, 4:31, and 4:32 affect wording, not the first-person reset.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should the pe-marked fulfillment hinge and the restored first-person doxology surface as children, and should WEB 4:28 hydrate backward as well as forward?

reviews.literary_form: feast disrupted by an unexplained writing
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The feast, vessel command, praise catalogue, sudden hand, royal terror, reward offer, and failed interpreters form one disrupted-court scene; the queen's entrance at 5:10 changes speaker and advisory function.
reviews.counterevidence: A samekh after 5:7 distinguishes the summons from the interpreters' failure, but both are phases of the unresolved sign scene.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 5:1-9; reject separating the vessel episode or hand from the failed-interpretation crisis.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 5:5, 5:7, and 5:8.
Titles, kinship language, vessels, and sign vocabulary do not authorize historical reconstruction.

reviews.literary_form: advisor recommendation and interpreter summons
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The queen enters because of the crisis, names Daniel's remembered competence, and prompts his arrival; the king then restates the same sign and reward request. The pe after 5:16 closes the summons before Daniel's answer.
reviews.counterevidence: A pe after 5:12 and the speaker change at 5:13 support subordinate queen-speech and king-speech children.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 5:10-16 as one interpreter-intake scene; if children are needed, hydrate 5:10-12 with 5:13-16.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 5:10, 5:13, 5:14, and 5:16.
Court titles and relationship terms remain translation evidence only.

reviews.literary_form: rebuke and sign interpretation followed by honor, death, and regnal transition
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: בֵּאדַיִן עָנֵה דָנִיֵּאל begins the answer; 5:24 introduces the writing, 5:29 returns to royal action, and 5:30 closes with a pe and the same-night death. WEB 5:31 is MT 6:1, a new MT chapter that also prepares the Darius tale.
reviews.counterevidence: WEB places 5:31 as the feast tale's coda, while MT places the same verse at the start of chapter 6. Correlated WLC views cannot independently resolve retrieval treatment.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Preserve alternatives Dan.5.17-28 plus 5:29-30 plus 5:31-6:3, or Dan.5.17-30 plus Dan.5.31-6.9; do not silently treat WEB versification as literary authority.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at MT 5:18, 5:19, 5:21-23, 5:29, and 5:30.
The writing's wordplay and royal identities are not adjudicated; no local OG/Theodotion apparatus is available.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should WEB 5:31/MT 6:1 close the feast tale, open the Darius tale, or be a bridge child with mandatory hydration to both?

reviews.literary_form: appointment, conspiracy, and signed-decree setup
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: WEB 6:1/MT 6:2 begins שְׁפַר קֳדָם דָּרְיָוֶשׁ and the appointments, investigation, collective petition, and signed writing. Daniel's response begins at WEB 6:10.
reviews.counterevidence: WEB 5:31/MT 6:1 supplies the regnal-receipt frame immediately before this unit, and the MT chapter begins there. The same correlated textual base supports both bridge treatment and the present WEB seam.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Preserve Dan.5.31-6.9 as an alternative setup parent; retain 6:1-9 only if 5:31 hydrates into it.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 6:1-9 maps to MT 6:2-10.
A samekh after MT 6:6/WEB 6:5 marks an internal conspiracy-to-petition turn, not necessarily a standalone chunk.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Must every retrieval of Dan.6.1-9 include the WEB 5:31/MT 6:1 transition verse?

reviews.literary_form: prayer counter-action, surveillance, accusation, and royal impasse
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְדָנִיֵּאל כְּדִי יְדַע introduces Daniel's response to the writing; discovery, prosecution, the king's rescue effort, and the accusers' legal closure form one counter-action scene before the command at 6:16.
reviews.counterevidence: A samekh after MT 6:11/WEB 6:10 can separate the prayer act from the accusers' observation, but the latter depends directly on the former.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain WEB 6:10-15; reject isolating 6:10 as a devotional proof text.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 6:10-15 maps to MT 6:11-16.
MT 6:14 carries correlated qere/ketiv pressure; law and prayer language does not authorize legal or devotional prescription.

reviews.literary_form: den peril, deliverance, reversal, proclamation, and coda
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: בֵּאדַיִן מַלְכָּא אֲמַר initiates the execution; sealing, royal vigil, morning return, Daniel's answer, extraction, counter-judgment, proclamation, and prosperity coda complete the peril-to-reversal arc.
reviews.counterevidence: The counter-judgment and decree are distinct closure phases and could be hydrated children, but separating them from the den outcome would remove their narrative cause.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain WEB 6:16-28; do not isolate the deliverance, violent reversal, decree, or coda.
translation_and_textual_risks: WEB 6:16-28 maps to MT 6:17-29.
Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at MT 6:17, 6:21, 6:23, 6:26, 6:27, and 6:29; no miracle, ethics, or historical conclusion follows.

reviews.literary_form: dated symbolic dream report
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The dated first-person dream superscription and repeated חָזֵה הֲוֵית progression carry sea, winds, four beasts, and horn focus until the throne-scene reset at 7:9.
reviews.counterevidence: Each beast could be indexed internally, but the cumulative symbolic register should not be atomized.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 7:1-8; reject one chunk per beast or horn.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 7:5-8.
No beast, horn, kingdom, person, chronology, or fulfillment identity is selected.

reviews.literary_form: heavenly-court vision and dominion grant
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: חָזֵה הֲוֵית עַד דִּי כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו resets the visual scene to thrones, court, books, judgment, cloud-borne approach, and dominion. The pe after 7:14 strongly closes the scene.
reviews.counterevidence: The beast's judgment at 7:11-12 relates backward to 7:1-8, so the complete 7:1-28 vision remains a parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 7:9-14; reject isolating 7:13-14 from the heavenly court.
translation_and_textual_risks: MT 7:10 carries correlated qere/ketiv pressure.
כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ is read within the vision syntax only; no identity, Christology, or fulfillment ruling is made.

reviews.literary_form: two-round interpretation dialogue and closing reaction
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: 7:15-18 contains distress, approach, request, and a concise four-beast interpretation. אֱדַיִן צְבִית לְיַצָּבָא at 7:19 begins a second, focused inquiry and extended answer through the explicit end formula at 7:28.
reviews.counterevidence: Both rounds interpret the same vision and must remain hydrated under the complete 7:1-28 parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer Dan.7.15-18 and Dan.7.19-28 as children; reject one undifferentiated interpretation block.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 7:19, 7:20, 7:23, and 7:25.
The time formula and figure identities remain unresolved; no independent versional source is local.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should the first general interpretation and the second focused inquiry be separate children with the whole vision mandatory?

reviews.literary_form: dated Hebrew symbolic vision with intravision question
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: בִּשְׁנַת שָׁלוֹשׁ and חָזוֹן נִרְאָה אֵלַי reopen in Hebrew after 7:28. The location, ram-goat-horn sequence, holy-one question, and numbered reply remain within the observed vision.
reviews.counterevidence: The intravision dialogue at 8:13-14 could be a child, but it depends on the sanctuary action just narrated.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 8:1-14; reject making the Hebrew return, each animal, each horn, or the number a standalone chunk.
translation_and_textual_risks: MT 8:11 carries correlated qere/ketiv pressure.
הַתָּמִיד, פַּלְמוֹנִי, and 2,300 evenings-mornings remain phrase-context evidence only; no calculation or fulfillment.

reviews.literary_form: messenger encounter and symbolic interpretation
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וַיְהִי בִּרְאֹתִי ... וָאֲבַקְשָׁה בִינָה initiates the interpretation encounter; commissioning voice, touch, temporal framing, symbol explanation, and sealing instruction form one response.
reviews.counterevidence: Touch/commission and exposition are internal movements, but splitting them would detach interpretive authority inside the scene.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 8:15-26 as the interpretation scene; do not split individual symbols or time expressions.
translation_and_textual_risks: No qere/ketiv tag occurs in the two correlated views for this span; absence is not evidence of wider textual stability.
Messenger, ruler, horn, sanctuary, number, chronology, and fulfillment identities remain deferred.

reviews.literary_form: vision-aftermath coda
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וַאֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל marks bodily illness, recovery, resumed royal work, astonishment, and lack of understanding; the pe after 8:27 closes the entire vision report.
reviews.counterevidence: The first-person coda is formally distinct, but it is not independently intelligible apart from the preceding vision and interpretation.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Merge 8:27 into Dan.8.15-27 for retrieval, or expose it only as a non-standalone child under Dan.8.1-27; reject an independently surfaced singleton.
translation_and_textual_risks: No local independent witness clarifies the aftermath wording.
The coda authorizes no medical, historical, or psychological inference.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should 8:27 exist only as a hydrated closure child, never as a standalone retrieval chunk?

reviews.literary_form: dated reading and prayer-orientation frame
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: The regnal frame, book-based understanding of Jeremiah's number, and וָאֶתְּנָה אֶת־פָּנַי prayer orientation prepare the direct prayer at 9:4.
reviews.counterevidence: The frame and prayer are causally joined, so Dan.9.1-19 remains a useful parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 9:1-3; reject isolating the seventy-years reference or merging the orientation into direct address.
translation_and_textual_risks: Regnal, seventy-year, and book language does not authorize historical harmonization or chronology.
No qere/ketiv tag occurs in the correlated views for this span.

reviews.literary_form: communal confessional prayer and urgent petition
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וָאֶתְפַּלְלָה ... וָאֶתְוַדֶּה opens direct address; first-person plural confession, covenant/curses language, exodus recollection, and repeated petitions continue through the closing imperative sequence at 9:19.
reviews.counterevidence: Confession, rationale, and petition are internal rhetorical movements, but they remain one uninterrupted prayer.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 9:4-19; reject proof-text isolation of individual confession or petition lines.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 9:5, 9:12, and 9:18.
Internal canonical wording is contextual evidence only, not automatic dependence, doctrine, or graph truth.

reviews.literary_form: prayer-response encounter and compressed temporal oracle
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְעוֹד אֲנִי מְדַבֵּר וּמִתְפַּלֵּל explicitly binds the arrival to the prayer; messenger arrival, insight command, and the seventy-weeks discourse continue to the pe after 9:27.
reviews.counterevidence: 9:24 begins a numbered oracle after the 9:20-23 encounter, but detaching it would remove the commissioned response frame.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 9:20-27; if 9:20-23 and 9:24-27 are indexed as children, require the complete answer parent and prohibit number atomization.
translation_and_textual_risks: MT 9:24 has correlated qere/ketiv pressure; שבעים שבעים, משיח, נחתך, antecedents, punctuation, and abomination/desolation wording remain unresolved.
No chronology, identity, fulfillment, preferred punctuation, or witness is selected.

reviews.literary_form: revelation superscription/mourning frame followed by river vision
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: 10:1 supplies date, name, message summary, and understanding; 10:2-3 gives the three-week mourning frame and ends with a pe. A new exact day and river location at 10:4 opens the overwhelming appearance through 10:9.
reviews.counterevidence: The mourning prepares the encounter, so Dan.10.1-9 remains a strong parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer Dan.10.1-3 and Dan.10.4-9 as hydrated children; reject crossing the pe and second date without acknowledging the scene reset.
translation_and_textual_risks: The phrase צָבָא גָדוֹל and vision/message terms are interpreted only in local syntax, not as chronology or history.
No qere/ketiv tag occurs in the correlated views for this span.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should the pe-marked mourning frame and separately dated river encounter be two retrievable children under the final-revelation parent?

reviews.literary_form: restoration dialogue followed by disclosure preface
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְהִנֵּה־יָד נָגְעָה בִּי begins repeated touch, raising, reassurance, and speech restoration through 10:19. וַיֹּאמֶר הֲיָדַעְתָּ at 10:20 begins the messenger's purpose/conflict preface; 11:1 continues the first-person speaker before וְעַתָּה אֱמֶת אַגִּיד at 11:2.
reviews.counterevidence: MT places a pe after 10:21 and a chapter boundary before 11:1, while syntax and speaker continuity link 11:1 backward. The complete 10:10-11:1 parent should remain available.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer Dan.10.10-19 and Dan.10.20-11.1 as children; preserve 10:20-11:1 as a contested cross-chapter disclosure preface rather than treating 10:21|11:1 as settled.
translation_and_textual_risks: No independent witness or apparatus is local to adjudicate the 10:21|11:1 attachment.
Princes, messenger identity, conflict, and historical referents remain deferred.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should 10:20-11:1 be a cross-chapter child despite the MT pe after 10:21, with 10:10-11:1 retained as parent?

reviews.literary_form: compressed succession and conflict register
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְעַתָּה אֱמֶת אַגִּיד לָךְ opens the disclosed sequence; repeated standing, direction, alliance, campaign, and succession clauses continue until the brief tax-collector successor at 11:20, after which 11:21 introduces a newly characterized successor.
reviews.counterevidence: Multiple rulers and campaigns permit internal indexing, but they function cumulatively and should not become event atoms.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 11:2-20; reject one chunk per king, campaign, marriage, or death.
translation_and_textual_risks: Correlated qere/ketiv tags occur at 11:10, 11:12, and 11:18.
Direction terms, ruler identity, event mapping, chronology, and fulfillment remain unresolved.

reviews.literary_form: escalating antagonist disclosure
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְעָמַד עַל־כַּנּוֹ נִבְזֶה introduces a newly characterized subject whose flatteries, conflict, covenant hostility, profanation, persecution, instruction, and refining-time refrain continue through 11:35.
reviews.counterevidence: Campaign and profanation clauses contain internal movements, but no local section marker or stronger speaker reset divides the sequence.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Retain 11:21-35; reject atomizing campaigns, covenant clauses, abomination language, or the wise.
translation_and_textual_risks: No qere/ketiv tag occurs in the correlated views for this span; this does not establish independent stability.
Actor, covenant, sanctuary, abomination, wise, history, chronology, and fulfillment remain deferred.

reviews.literary_form: renewed royal portrait and campaign climax
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְעָשָׂה כִרְצוֹנוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ at 11:36 is a strong subject-and-action restart; the exaltation, worship/power clauses, time-of-end conflict, alarms, tents, and unassisted end continue through 11:45.
reviews.counterevidence: The text supplies no named new actor, no MT section marker at 11:35, and 12:1 begins וּבָעֵת הַהִיא, tightly continuing the temporal scene. Current correlated witnesses cannot decide continuation versus pivot or the 11:45|12:1 retrieval seam.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Preserve Dan.11.21-45 and Dan.11.36-12.4 as exact alternatives; do not decide by ruler identity, historical mapping, or fulfillment.
translation_and_textual_risks: MT 11:39 carries correlated qere/ketiv pressure.
No local OG/Theodotion/Qumran or independent versional source is available to test wording, order, or attachment.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Does the syntactic restart at 11:36 outweigh the unnamed-subject continuity, and should the unit continue through 12:4 because of וּבָעֵת הַהִיא?

reviews.literary_form: temporal culmination, wisdom coda, and sealing command
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וּבָעֵת הַהִיא at 12:1 explicitly continues the preceding time-of-end disclosure. MT places a samekh after 12:2 and a pe after 12:3; וְאַתָּה דָנִיֵּאל at 12:4 directly addresses Daniel with the sealing command.
reviews.counterevidence: Deliverance, awakening, the wise, and sealing form a coherent culmination, so 12:1-4 remains a useful child within the 10:1-12:13 parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Do not treat the chapter boundary as a clean start. Prefer a parent Dan.11.36-12.4, with possible children Dan.12.1-2, Dan.12.3, and Dan.12.4 only if hydration prevents proof-texting.
translation_and_textual_risks: The syntax of 12:2, the wise at 12:3, and sealing at 12:4 remain phrase-context evidence only.
No resurrection doctrine, identity, chronology, eschatology, or fulfillment is decided.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should Dan.12.1-4 remain independently retrievable, or only appear as the culmination of Dan.11.36-12.4 with section-marked internal children?

reviews.literary_form: two-round closing vision dialogue and personal dismissal
reviews.hebrew_aramaic_discourse_evidence: וְרָאִיתִי אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל at 12:5 opens the riverbank tableau and 'how long' exchange. At 12:8 Daniel asks a second question; a pe closes that verse, and וַיֹּאמֶר לֵךְ דָּנִיֵּאל at 12:9 begins the final answer, numbered periods, and repeated personal dismissal through 12:13.
reviews.counterevidence: Both exchanges share the river vision and closing commission, so Dan.12.5-13 remains a mandatory parent.
reviews.rejected_or_alternate_seam: Prefer Dan.12.5-8 and Dan.12.9-13 as hydrated children; never isolate 1,290 or 1,335 days from the full second answer.
translation_and_textual_risks: Time, times, half; 1,290; and 1,335 are preserved as discourse expressions, not calculated schedules.
No speaker identity, resurrection system, chronology, eschatology, or fulfillment is selected.
reviews.hot_zone_question: Should the pe after 12:8 govern two closing-dialogue children with the full 12:5-13 parent mandatory?
